questions.question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because its surface is covered in iron oxide, which is basically rust!
questions.funFact: Mars has the largest volcano in the entire solar system, called Olympus Mons!

questions.question: What is the scientific name for the process of a caterpillar turning into a butterfly?
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis means a major change in form, like how a caterpillar changes into a butterfly.
questions.funFact: Frogs also go through metamorphosis, changing from tadpoles into adult frogs!

questions.question: What invisible force pulls objects toward the center of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the pulling force that keeps our feet on the ground and the planets orbiting the sun.
questions.funFact: If you weigh 100 pounds on Earth, you would only weigh about 38 pounds on Mars due to lower gravity!

questions.question: Which part of a plant is mainly responsible for making food using sunlight?
questions.explanation: Leaves catch sunlight and use it to turn water and air into food for the plant.
questions.funFact: Giant water lily leaves can grow over 10 feet across and hold the weight of a small child!

questions.question: What state of matter is water when it takes the shape of its container but doesn't fill it completely?
questions.explanation: Liquids like water and juice flow and take the shape of the cup you pour them into.
questions.funFact: Water is the only natural substance found in all three states (solid, liquid, gas) at normal Earth temperatures!

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance found on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamonds are formed deep underground under extreme heat and pressure, making them super hard.
questions.funFact: Diamonds are so hard that the only natural thing that can scratch a diamond is another diamond!

questions.question: What kind of animal has fur or hair and feeds its babies milk?
questions.explanation: Mammals are warm-blooded animals with hair or fur, and they produce milk for their young.
questions.funFact: Even though they live in the ocean, whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish!

questions.question: What is the very hot, liquid rock found deep inside the Earth or a volcano called?
questions.explanation: Melted rock underground is called magma. When it erupts above ground, it is called lava.
questions.funFact: Lava can reach temperatures over 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,200 degrees Celsius)!

questions.question: What covers about 70 percent of the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The Earth is sometimes called the 'Blue Planet' because oceans of water cover most of it.
questions.funFact: More than 80% of the Earth's oceans have never been mapped or explored by humans!

questions.question: Which important human organ pumps blood all throughout the body?
questions.explanation: The heart acts like a pump, pushing oxygen-rich blood through your blood vessels.
questions.funFact: Your heart beats about 100,000 times in one single day!

questions.question: What gas do we breathe out that plants need to survive?
questions.explanation: Animals breathe out carbon dioxide, and plants use it to make food, releasing oxygen back for us!
questions.funFact: Without plants taking in carbon dioxide, Earth would get way too hot for us to live on!

questions.question: What type of simple machine is a playground seesaw?
questions.explanation: A lever is a stiff bar that rests on a support called a fulcrum, just like a seesaw.
questions.funFact: Ancient Egyptians used huge levers to help build the massive pyramids!

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and it is much closer to us than any other star in the universe.
questions.funFact: The Sun is so huge that you could fit over one million Earths inside it!

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants are known as what?
questions.explanation: Herbivores, like deer, cows, and rabbits, get all their energy from eating plants.
questions.funFact: The largest animal to ever live on land, the Argentinosaurus, was a gentle herbivore!

questions.question: What special chemical gives plants their green color?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll makes plants green and helps them trap sunlight for photosynthesis.
questions.funFact: Sea slugs can eat algae and use the algae's chlorophyll to make food from sunlight, just like a plant!

questions.question: What are clouds mostly made of?
questions.explanation: When water vapor in the air cools down, it forms tiny liquid water drops or ice crystals, creating clouds.
questions.funFact: A single puffy cumulus cloud can weigh as much as 100 elephants!

questions.question: How long does it take for the Earth to travel all the way around the Sun?
questions.explanation: It takes the Earth about 365 days, or one year, to complete one orbit around the Sun.
questions.funFact: Because it actually takes 365 and a quarter days, we add an extra day every four years, called Leap Year!

questions.question: What do we call a scientist who studies stars, planets, and space?
questions.explanation: Astronomers use telescopes and satellites to look at things far away in the universe.
questions.funFact: Galileo was an early astronomer who discovered that Jupiter has its own moons!

questions.question: Which of these materials is pulled by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract certain metals, like iron, steel, and nickel.
questions.funFact: The Earth itself is actually a giant magnet with a North and South magnetic pole!

questions.question: What do we call a heavy wind storm that is shaped like a spinning funnel?
questions.explanation: Tornadoes are violent, rotating columns of air that touch the ground.
questions.funFact: Tornado winds can spin faster than 300 miles per hour!
